items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to the implementation of an
electronic death registration system
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7630

SPONSOR: YOUNG
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public health law, in relation to
the implementation of an electronic death registration system

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To set a hard and fast date for full implementation and use of the NYS
Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS), and to end, on that same
date, the $20 fee paid by funeral directors on each burial permit to
fund the EDRS system.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 4140 of the NYS Public Health Law is amended in Section 1 of the
bill to make a conforming change to ensure the electronic filing of
death certificates; Section 4148 of the Public Health Law is amended in
Section 2 to provide that the EDRS system must be fully implemented by
the 60th day after this legislation is enacted, which shall be the
"implementation date"; eliminates the payment collected from funeral
firms to finance the EDRS system on the same date; Clarifies that any
person violating the requirements to use the EDRS system shall be
subject to existing penalties as provided in the Public Health Law; and,
removes language that would permit further slippage for implementation
beyond the "implementation date"; Section 4171 of the Public Health Law
is amended in Section 3 to make a further conforming and clarifying
change to state that no death certificate shall be complete and correct
that is not filed electronically as required; and, Section 4 sets forth
the effective date of the bill.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The legal and practical responsibility for coordinating the current
manual process of ensuring the completion and filing of each death
certificate within 72 hours after a death falls upon funeral directors.
The very cumbersome and time-consuming nature of this process needlessly
takes valuable time away from a funeral director that could, and should,
be dedicated to serving the needs of those who have just suffered the
loss of a cherished family member or other loved one. As a result, a law
was enacted in 2013 to require the development and implementation of a
NYS EDRS with funeral firms stepping forward to agree to fund this
system. (Such systems are already being fully used in New York City,
which has its own system, and in most states). The 2013 law required
implementation of NYS EDRS by January 1, 2015.

While progress has been made in some quarters of the state to fully
implement EDRS, it is evident that certain stakeholders in various parts
of the state have not prioritized converting to EDRS from the archaic
manual system. The process of filing death certificates requires the
active collaboration of many parties, and, without the commitment and
participation of all these important parties, EDRS simply cannot fully
be implemented and serve as intended. This is especially frustrating to
funeral directors, who continue to finance EDRS through a statutorily-
mandated $20 fee for each burial permit issued to them - even though the
system is not yet close to being fully implemented.

This bill improves upon the original law by setting a specific, hard
date for "full implementation" of EDRS throughout the State as no later
than 60 days following enactment of this Act; ensures that penalties
will be assessed by DOH on any party who is not fully compliant with
EDRS usage requirements by that date; and, removes the $20 burial permit
fee on funeral firms that have been paying since 2013 and which have not
yet been able to fully see the promise of an EDRS system.

The State has collected approximately $8 million since 2013 from funeral
firms to develop and implement EDRS, well more than enough to do so. In
addition, birth certificates have been filed electronically in NYS for
several years. It is well past time to ensure EDRS is fully implemented
as well as to provide financial relief to our State's funeral homes,
which have single-handedly paid for this system for almost five years.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

The $20 fee assessed paid by funeral homes for each burial permit would
be removed, but the approximately $8 million contributed since 2013 is
more than needed to develop and implement NYS EDRS.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

BILL NUMBER: S7630A

SPONSOR: YOUNG
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to the implementation
of an electronic death registration system

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To set a hard and fast effective date of 1/1/2019 for full implementa-
tion of and use of the NYS Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS)
and to assess penalties for those not in compliance effective 1/1/2019
unless the Department of Health determines that non-compliance is
attributable to a circumstance or occurrence beyond the control of an
individual.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Section 4140 of the NYS Public Health Law is amended to make
a conforming change to ensure the electronic filing of death certif-
icates;

Section 2. Section 4148 of the Public Health Law is amended to provide
that the EDRS system must be fully implemented effective January 1,
2019; Clarifies that any person violating the requirements to use the
EDRS system shall be subject to existing penalties as provided in the
Public Health Law; and, removes language that would permit further slip-
page for implementation beyond the "implementation date"; adds language
to allow for the department to waive penalties should it be determined
that non-compliance is attributable to a circumstance or occurrence
beyond the control of an individual;

Section 3. Section 4171 of the Public Health Law is amended to make a
further conforming and clarifying change to state that no death certif-
icate shall be complete and correct that is not filed electronically as
required; and, Section 4 sets forth the effective date of the bill.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The legal and practical responsibility for coordinating the current

This bill improves upon the original law by setting a specific, hard
date for "full implementation" of EDRS throughout the State as no later
than January 1, 2019; ensures that penalties will be assessed by DOH on
any party who is not fully compliant with EDRS usage requirements by
that date; and, allows DOH to waive penalties should it be determined
that the noncompliance is attributable to a circumstance or occurrence
beyond the control of an individual.

The State has collected approximately $8 million since 2013 from funeral
firms to develop and implement EDRS, well more than enough to do so. In
addition, birth certificates have been filed electronically in NYS for

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7630B

SPONSOR: YOUNG
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public health law, in relation to
the implementation of an electronic death registration system

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To provide that fees charged prospectively to fund the establishment and
use of the NYS Electronic Death Registration System (EDRS)shall only be
collected in instances where the death certificate is actually issued
electronically.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Subdivisions one and five of Section 4148 of the Public
Health Law are amended to provide that the fee established to fund the
EDRS system need only be paid in instances where the death certificate
is actually electronically issued to a funeral director.

Section 2. Provides that this act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The legal and practical responsibility for coordinating the current
manual process of ensuring the completion and filing of each death
certificate within 72 hours after a death falls upon funeral directors.
The very cumbersome and time-consuming nature of this process needlessly
takes valuable time away from a funeral director that could, and should,
be dedicated to serving the needs of those who have just suffered the
loss of a cherished family member or other loved one. As a result, a law
was enacted in 2013 to require the development and implementation of a
NYS EDRS with funeral firms stepping forward to agree to fund this
system. (Such systems are already being fully used in New York City,
which has its own system, and in most states). The 2013 law required
implementation of NYS EDRS by January 1, 2015.

While progress has been made in some quarters of the state to fully
implement EDRS, it is evident that certain stakeholders in various parts
of the state have not prioritized converting to EDRS from the archaic
manual system. The process of filing death certificates requires the
active collaboration of many parties, and, without the commitment and
participation of all these important parties, EDRS simply cannot fully
be implemented and serve as intended.

This bill improves upon the original law by providing that in the future
"implementation" of EDRS throughout the state the users of the system
shall only be assessed the EDRS implementation fee when they are actual-
ly issued a permit pursuant to the EDRS system.

The State has collected approximately $8 million since 2013 from funeral
firms to develop and implement EDRS, well more than enough to do so. In
addition, birth certificates have been filed electronically in NYS for
several years. This bill will serve as an encouragement for the full
implementation of EDRS.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.
 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to state if EDRS is enacted as originally required in statute.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

summary: Relates to the implementation of an electronic death registration system; provides that a payment shall be collected for each burial or removal permit issued electronically.
